product_offering.core_offering: Videa sells a subscription-based dental AI platform that combines FDA-cleared X-ray diagnostics, ambient AI scribing for clinical documentation, and automated revenue cycle management workflows for dental practices and Dental Support Organizations. The platform unifies Clinical Assist, Voice Notes, Voice Perio, Daily Dashboard, Insights, Clean Claims, AutoVerify, and ClaimsAI into a single solution sold via annual SaaS subscriptions.
product_offering.differentiator: Most adopted dental AI platform in dentistry with 90,000+ clinicians. 35 FDA-cleared detections (more than double any competitor). Fastest deployment capability - rolled out to 1,500+ practices in under 10 weeks. Only platform covering full dental workflow from diagnostics to revenue cycle management. Strong DSO relationships with 8 of 10 largest DSOs.
product_offering.functional_benefit: 20% higher case acceptance rates; 1-2 hours saved per clinician daily; 50% reduction in insurance claim denials; 12% increase in patient treatment acceptance; improved diagnostic accuracy with AI-assisted X-ray analysis; automated clinical documentation; real-time practice analytics; streamlined insurance verification
product_offering.problem_solved: Dental practices struggle with diagnostic inconsistency across providers, excessive administrative burden (documentation, insurance verification, claims), low patient case acceptance rates, and difficulty scaling operations across multiple locations. Videa addresses these by providing AI-assisted diagnostics, automated documentation, streamlined insurance workflows, and practice analytics.

product_offering.product_overview: Videa is a comprehensive dental AI platform that offers a unified suite of integrated products for dental practices and Dental Service Organizations (DSOs). The platform architecture includes Clinical Assist (core diagnostic AI with X-ray analysis and patient visualization), Voice Notes (ambient AI scribe for clinical documentation), Voice Perio (hands-free periodontal charting), Daily Dashboard (AI-powered treatment opportunity identification), Insights (clinical analytics and performance benchmarking), Clean Claims (automated claims processing), and AutoVerify (insurance eligibility verification). The platform is built on a proprietary FDA-cleared AI engine that analyzes over 500 million X-rays annually and is deployed across over 90,000 clinicians at 60+ leading DSOs. The platform connects diagnostics, documentation, and daily operations for the chair, front desk, and practice management.

product_and_service.description: AI-powered diagnostic support tool that analyzes dental X-rays in real time, highlights conditions such as caries, calculus, and periapical radiolucency, and generates colorized patient-friendly visualizations to improve case acceptance and clinical confidence. expansion_highlight.description: April 2026 rebrand from VideaHealth to Videa explicitly extends go-to-market from large DSOs to independent private dental practices, materially widening the addressable customer base from a few hundred enterprise accounts to hundreds of thousands of SMB practices.
Geographic expansion into Canada via 123Dentist (400+ clinics nationwide) and 2025 Series B funding earmarked for market expansion indicate active internationalization beyond the US core.

Product surface expansion from diagnostics (Clinical Assist) into ambient documentation (Voice Notes Oct 2025, Voice Perio), revenue cycle management (ClaimsAI July 2025, AutoVerify Jan 2026), and conversational intelligence (Ambient Intelligence May 2026) signals a deliberate platform breadth strategy covering the full chair-to-claim workflow.

Embedded distribution partnership with Henry Schein One inside Dentrix and Dentrix Ascend (Nov 2025) creates a channel-led motion that bypasses direct sales friction and unlocks the long tail of practices on those PMS platforms.

$40M oversubscribed Series B led by Threshold Ventures (Jan 2025) explicitly earmarked for platform scaling, geographic expansion, and product broadening — a clear funding-signal of expansion capacity.

Launch of the AI Leadership Council (Jan 2026) — with CMOs/CSOs from Aspen, Heartland, 42 North, Gen4, Riccobene, Cherry Tree, and Great Expressions — and partnership with the Dentist Entrepreneur Organization (DEO, Jan 2026) constitute ecosystem buildout designed to entrench category standards and shape buyer preference.

company_assessment.market_position: Videa (legal entity Videa Health, Inc., founded 2018 out of MIT by Florian Hillen, headquartered in Boston, MA) is the most adopted dental AI platform in North America, used by 90,000+ clinicians across 60+ leading Dental Support Organizations (DSOs) including 8 of North America's 10 largest DSOs and 80%+ of the top 10 dental networks. The company rebranded from VideaHealth to Videa in April 2026 when it expanded go-to-market beyond enterprise DSOs to independent private dental practices. It has raised $60M+ across Series A and Series B rounds led by Spark Capital and Threshold Ventures, respectively.

strengths.details: Videa has evolved from a single-feature X-ray detector to a unified platform spanning Clinical Assist, Voice Notes, Voice Perio, Daily Dashboard, Insights, Clean Claims, AutoVerify, ClaimsAI, and the new Ambient Intelligence category. Each new module layers onto the same FDA-cleared engine and embedded Dentrix deployment, turning each practice into a multi-product account and materially expanding ARR per site over time.
strengths.headline: Platform expansion from diagnostics to full revenue cycle unlocks massive wallet share.

strengths.details: With 500M+ X-rays analyzed annually and ~90,000 clinicians feeding real-world feedback, Videa's training corpus and benchmarking insights (e.g., Insights product) widen every quarter — a flywheel that is structurally hard for late entrants to replicate and should drive widening accuracy advantages and stickier renewals.
strengths.headline: Data-network effects compound with every X-ray analyzed at scale.

strengths.details: One-click activation inside Dentrix and Dentrix Ascend positions Videa as the default AI layer across the largest PMS installed base. As the April 2026 rebrand opens the independent-practice segment, this embedment should drive low-CAC land-and-expand into tens of thousands of additional practices without a proportionate salesforce expansion.
strengths.headline: Embedded Henry Schein One partnership unlocks the long tail of independent practices.

strengths.details: Clean Claims and AutoVerify target claim denials (50% reduction in early results) and eligibility verification (95%+ payer coverage), addressing roughly $15B in dental RCM waste per company commentary. Scaling these modules converts Videa from a clinical-AI vendor into a margin-recovery platform, materially expanding the revenue envelope per customer.
strengths.headline: AI-led revenue cycle management attacks a large, under-digitized dental RCM market.

strengths.details: North American DSOs are rapidly consolidating, and Videa already covers 8 of the 10 largest networks. As those customers grow via M&A and as Tier-2/3 DSOs professionalize, Videa's proven multi-week enterprise rollout playbook (Aspen 6 weeks, Heartland 10 weeks, Great Expressions 2 weeks) should translate into faster, larger enterprise wins with limited incremental go-to-market cost.
strengths.headline: DSO consolidation tailwind accelerates both land and expand.

weakness.details: With Aspen and Heartland alone representing ~2,600+ practices of Videa's footprint, any multi-year renewal reset, in-house AI build, or partial rollout contraction at these accounts would compress revenue and operating leverage in lockstep — a vulnerability that grows as the company adds fewer, larger customers before broader diversification.
weakness.headline: Mega-DSO renewals concentrate revenue risk at scale.

weakness.details: Videa's 35 FDA-cleared detections are described as more than double any competitor, but competitors such as Pearl and Overjet are steadily accumulating clearances of their own. Once a rival approaches parity on detection breadth and accuracy, pricing power, win rates, and renewal economics will all come under pressure.
weakness.headline: Competitor parity on FDA clearances could erode the '2x' moat.

weakness.details: The April 2026 pivot to independent practices requires a fundamentally different sales motion (low-touch, demo-driven, likely smaller average contract values) than the existing DSO field-sales engine. If SMB conversion lags or churn rises, customer acquisition costs could balloon before unit economics mature, compressing margins even as headline clinician count grows.
weakness.headline: Independent-practice expansion could dilute margins on an unproven SMB motion.

weakness.details: Embedded Dentrix and Dentrix Ascend integrations are core to Videa's go-to-market; a strategic dispute, exclusivity shift to a rival AI vendor, or material change in Henry Schein One's AI roadmap could simultaneously affect activation, upsell, and competitive positioning across a large portion of Videa's installed base.
weakness.headline: Henry Schein One channel concentration is a single point of failure.

weakness.details: As Videa pushes into higher-risk categories — Ambient Intelligence, AI-driven revenue cycle decisions, OrthoAI/ImplantAI — it will face more demanding FDA, payer, and clinical-oversight scrutiny. Any forced re-clearance, post-market surveillance event, or new AI-specific rules could delay launches and raise compliance costs at exactly the moment the company is scaling into new modules.
weakness.headline: Increasing AI and SaMD regulatory scrutiny could slow product velocity.

competitive_moat.details: Videa's AI analyzes 500M+ dental X-rays annually, creating an unparalleled proprietary training dataset that compounds with scale and is not replicable by new entrants. This data flywheel underpins the 35 FDA-cleared detections — more than double any other dental AI vendor.

Embedded inside Henry Schein One's Dentrix and Dentrix Ascend platforms, plus integrations with OpenDental, Patterson, Planet DDS, SOTA Dental, ClearDent, and Dentsply Sirona, Videa reaches the installed base of major practice management systems. 8 of North America's 10 largest DSOs and 60+ leading DSOs are deployed, representing 80%+ of the top 10 dental networks.

35 FDA-cleared detections for dental conditions (caries, calculus, periapical radiolucency, and others) constitute a regulatory moat requiring clinical validation that competitors must replicate, doubling the next-best vendor's count.

Deep integration with practice management systems (Dentrix, OpenDental, Patterson, Trinity), workflow embedding at chairside and front desk, and clinician training on AI-assisted diagnostics create meaningful friction — sustained 95% usage rate evidences stickiness.

90,000+ active clinicians generate continuous usage data and clinical feedback that improve detection accuracy and template coverage (e.g., 35+ Voice Notes procedure templates), producing a learning flywheel that benefits existing and new customers.

MIT-originated brand pedigree, clinical leadership via the AI Leadership Council with CMOs/CSOs of major DSOs (Aspen, Heartland, 42 North, Gen4), and a 2025 Inc. 5000 rank of #28 (highest of any dental organization in any category) reinforce category leadership.

key_risks.details: Just two customers (Aspen Dental at 1,100+ practices and Heartland Dental at 1,500+ practices) account for a very large share of deployed endpoints. Loss or downsizing of either account would materially impact revenue and operating leverage.
key_risks.headline: Heavy customer concentration in a few mega-DSOs creates renewal and churn concentration risk.

key_risks.details: Companies such as Pearl and Overjet are pursuing the same dental imaging AI category with similar FDA-clearance roadmaps; differentiation must be defended continuously, and competitor parity on detection count could erode the current '2x' advantage over time.
key_risks.headline: Crowded competitive landscape in dental AI from well-funded rivals.

key_risks.details: Significant go-to-market leverage flows through Dentrix/Dentrix Ascend; a Henry Schein One strategy shift, pricing dispute, or competing AI partnership could compress Videa's activation funnel and embedment in core PMS workflows.
key_risks.headline: Distribution dependency on Henry Schein One's Dentrix ecosystem is a structural channel risk.

key_risks.details: The April 2026 rebrand explicitly expanded Videa from large DSOs to independent private practices, moving from field-sales to high-velocity SMB sales without historical traction data — execution risk on unit economics and CAC in a fragmented long-tail market.
key_risks.headline: New SMB / independent-practice GTM is unproven after a long enterprise-only focus.

key_risks.details: Operating at 51–100 employees while serving 90,000+ clinicians, 1,500+ practices at the largest customer, and multiple regulated SaaS products elevates concentration risk on founder/CEO Florian Hillen and limits resilience if key clinical or regulatory staff depart.
key_risks.headline: Key-person and founder dependency with very lean headcount for the operational footprint.

key_risks.details: Sales depend on continuing to hold FDA clearances across an expanding set of detections; any future adverse event report, recall, or tightening of FDA's SaMD/AI/ML oversight framework could disrupt launches such as Ambient Intelligence and upcoming AI capabilities.
key_risks.headline: Regulatory and clinical-liability exposure from being an FDA-regulated SaMD.

key_highlights.details: Videa is used by 90,000+ active clinicians at 60+ leading DSOs and processes 500M+ X-rays annually. This scale provides both a defensible training-data advantage and embedded workflow presence.
key_highlights.headline: Massive clinical user base of 90,000+ active clinicians across 60+ DSOs creates a strong data and distribution moat.

key_highlights.details: Videa's Clinical Assist has 35 FDA-cleared dental condition detections (caries, calculus, periapical radiolucency, etc.), explicitly described as more than double any other AI vendor in dentistry. This regulatory barrier is hard for competitors to match quickly.
key_highlights.headline: Regulatory moat: 35 FDA-cleared AI detections, more than double any competing dental AI vendor.

key_highlights.details: Including deployments at Aspen Dental (1,100+ practices), Heartland Dental (1,500+ practices), and Great Expressions (210+ practices). 80%+ of the 10 largest North American dental networks are on Videa — exceptional distribution depth.
key_highlights.headline: Deep enterprise entrenchment: 8 of North America's 10 largest DSOs run on Videa.

key_highlights.details: Customers report 46% more cavities detected, 10% drop in diagnostic errors, 20% higher case acceptance, 50% reduction in claim denials, and $78,268 average additional annual revenue per practice with 95% sustained usage — compelling payback that supports expansion and renewals.
key_highlights.headline: Quantified, strong customer ROI drives high sustained usage and case-acceptance lift.

key_highlights.details: Videa deployed to 1,500+ Heartland Dental practices in under 10 weeks, 1,100+ Aspen Dental practices in 6 weeks, and 210+ Great Expressions practices in 2 weeks — execution speed that materially lowers customer onboarding friction.
key_highlights.headline: Record-time enterprise rollouts prove operational excellence and product readiness.

key_highlights.details: Raised $40M Series B (Nov 2025) led by Threshold Ventures with participation from Avenir, BAM Corner Point, Spark Capital, Zetta Venture Partners, and Pillar VC, on top of $20M Series A in 2022 — total ~$60M raised with the round explicitly described as oversubscribed.
key_highlights.headline: Strong capital base with oversubscribed Series B led by a top-tier growth investor.

key_highlights.details: Videa is embedded directly within Dentrix and Dentrix Ascend via Henry Schein One, plus integrations with OpenDental, Patterson, SOTA Dental, Dentsply Sirona, ClearDent, and Planet DDS — one-click AI activation across the dominant PMS installed base in North America.
key_highlights.headline: Embedded partnership with Henry Schein One creates a structural distribution moat.

customer_concentration.details: Customer base is anchored by a small number of very large DSO contracts: Heartland Dental (1,500+ practices), Aspen Dental (1,100+ practices), 123Dentist (400+ clinics), Great Expressions (210+ practices), plus 8 of the 10 largest North American DSOs collectively. While 90,000+ clinicians provide a wide user footprint, the revenue concentration sits with the top enterprise DSO logos, and 80%+ of the top 10 dental networks depend on Videa. The April 2026 rebrand explicitly addresses this risk by opening the independent-practice long tail, but until that motion matures, churn or contraction at any top-3 DSO would represent material revenue exposure.
